redTeam.evidence: One public pain account and this synthetic founder report.
redTeam.inference: Retrieving rationale may be more useful than another comparison table.
redTeam.assumption: Recording effort is smaller than the later benefit.
redTeam.contradiction: Other users prefer existing notes; incumbents already compare and journal.
redTeam.disproof: An existing note template resolves the problem with no remaining friction.
redTeam.cheapestLearning: After evaluation, inspect a recent decision with the founder or discuss a recent example with a consenting relevant user.

master.thesis: Help this personal user preserve reasoning before claiming a commercial opportunity.
master.interviewPlan: Ask about the hardest part, last occurrence, why it was hard, attempted solutions and dislikes; follow the actual answer. Do not pitch or ask hypothetical buying questions.
master.mvpHypothesis: Only if chosen: capture a short rationale and retrieve it next to a consistent comparison.
master.technicalStrategy: Use the existing project stack if supplied; a local fictional-data example can test interaction without buying data.
master.businessModel: Personal usefulness first. Selling later remains a separate untested choice.
master.economics: No revenue model or margin claimed. Current data licensing, reliability and support costs must be investigated if commercialization is chosen.
master.validationPlan: Separate technical correctness from usefulness: review whether rationale is recovered with less repeated work. No market-validation claim from public pages.

brief.summary: The comparison space is already well served. A more useful personal angle may be remembering why you preferred one candidate, although a consistent spreadsheet note could be enough. One public discussion describes that memory problem; it does not establish a business.

Payment, prevalence and any investment-performance benefit remain unknown.
